# Builds the website and the documentation and publishes them as one GitHub
# Pages site: the website at the root, the documentation under /docs.
#
# GitHub Pages serves one site per repository with one custom domain, which is
# why these are combined rather than deployed separately. Splitting them later
# means pointing a second host at apps/docs; nothing in the repository layout
# has to change for that.
name: Deploy site

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Never let two deployments race; queue instead of cancelling, so a merged
# change is never dropped.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build both sites
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm

      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # The same script developers run locally.
      - name: Build and assemble both sites
        run: ./scripts/build-site.sh

      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v6
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: _site

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to Pages
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5
